input.question: Why do large semis shake your car when you drive past them?
input.ground_truth: [Vortex shedding](_URL_0_) Because semi's are not very streamlined the air rushing past them ends up in a series of vortices. As these vortices pass you, your car is alternately sucked toward and blown away from--hence the shaking motion.

Question: Why do large semis shake your car when you drive past them?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a little toy car, and next to you is a big, big truck. When the big truck drives by, it makes the ground shake a little because it is so heavy. 

When you are in your real car and a big semi (that’s a really big truck) drives by, it pushes a lot of air and makes the ground move just a tiny bit. That tiny movement makes your car wiggle or shake a little bit too, like when you jump on the bed and it bounces!

So, the big truck is so heavy and moves so much air that it makes your car shake a little when you drive next to it.
